title: ProviderContextManifest byom source fields (DESIGN.md §12.1, §16.6 item 5; Δ5)
description: The exact byom source fields §16.6 item 5 adds to Kovee's ProviderContextManifest, transcribed from §12.1's normative sentence: byom_endpoint, Society, Participant and binding epoch, ActivityStream, Episode/attempt/fence, ContextManifest ref/digest, ordered source-item refs and digests, classification-overlay digest, purpose, MandateUse refs, disclosure ceiling, omissions, and authorization-dependency digest. §12.1 names the members in prose, not as a field block, so the member names here are derived (slice-1 DPC honesty; recorded in the slice-2 gap notes). This is a source-relation FRAGMENT, not a record: Kovee alone owns the ProviderContextManifest and the final provider-visible ordering and bytes (system/assistant instructions, tool schemas, wrappers, transformations, provider binding, final outbound-byte digest); no convenience context may be appended outside Kovee's final manifest chain. ByomEpisodeBinding.context_source_digest is the digest over exactly this canonical fragment.

byom_endpoint_ref.description: §12.1 names this member `byom_endpoint`; suffixed _ref for consistency with the §16.6 binding block (derived-name note in the gap notes).

context_manifest_ref.description: The Episode's immutable byom ContextManifest (§12.1); possession grants nothing — materialization rechecks current authority.

ordered_source_items.description: Ordered source-item refs and digests (§12.1); order is byom's source order — Kovee owns the final provider-visible ordering.

disclosure_ceiling_ref.description: The disclosure ceiling governing what may reach the provider (§13.3).

explicit_omissions.description: Explicitly omitted inputs under current policy (§12.1): an erased or revoked input fails materialization; a new manifest may omit it explicitly, never silently.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.
